assumptions.obligation: The environment keeps i_cmd_valid at 0 whenever i_rst_n is 0. This is a combinational constraint, so it holds at every time step of reset.
i_rst_n is driven to 0 from time zero for at least the first 2 i_clk cycles (power-on reset). Later resets have no minimum length.

notes:
I left these obligations out on purpose:
(1) Mode inputs (SPI-5-14, SPI-5-16, SPI-12-04). The spec asks the environment to change i_cpol and i_cpha only while o_cs_n = 1. But SPI-12-05 allows error tests to break this rule, and SPI-7.3-03, SPI-10-02 and SPI-14-09 say what the master must do when it happens: ignore the change and keep CPOL_b and CPHA_b until the end of the burst. Assuming the rule would hide bugs in that capture logic, so i_cpol and i_cpha are left free. Changes during reset or Idle are legal anyway (SPI-12-28, SPI-6.2-03).
(2) Reset timing (SPI-5-01, SPI-12-01, SPI-12-02, SPI-12-10). Release synchronous to i_clk, and assertion between edges, are built into a single-clock formal model, so they need no assumption.
(3) i_miso (SPI-12-06 to SPI-12-09, SPI-12-15). These rules describe the testbench slave model and physical setup/hold, not a protocol obligation. Leaving i_miso free each cycle lets the properties catch sampling at the wrong edge (SPI-7.6-01 to SPI-7.6-04).
(4) Command stream. No stability or hold-until-ready assumptions, because SPI-12-16 says stability is not required. No limit on gaps, because Pause has no timeout (SPI-7.8-04).
(5) i_rsp_ready is unconstrained (SPI-12-17); back-pressure for any length of time is legal.
(6) The X/Z rule (SPI-12-13) is built into a 2-valued formal model.
(7) The helper counter for ENV-02 is deliberately not cleared by i_rst_n, because it only tracks the power-on reset from time zero.
